When receiving serve, watch the server's racket face and be ready to move either direction. A split-second's hesitation can cost you the point. Keep your returns deep and to the corners whenever possible, forcing your opponent to retrieve from a weak position rather than allowing them to attack comfortably.

In rallying, vary your shots deliberately. Mix topspin with slice, lobs with drives, and always be thinking two or three shots ahead. If your opponent has dragged you wide to the forehand, try a sharp cross-court return rather than attempting the difficult down-the-line pass—probability favours the cross-court angle.

Above all, condition yourself physically. The fitter player often wins, particularly in close matches. Run regularly, practise your footwork, and build your endurance. Technical skill will only take you so far without the stamina to execute when fatigue sets in in those crucial final games.

pair.human_continuation:
Keep your opponent wondering where the
service will come next; vary it as much as you possibly can, both as to
pace and direction. Be sure to make your opponent move to take it.

I have tried the American service, but I think the strain is too severe
for the average girl, and the advantage gained would be very slight, for
the rest of your game would deteriorate, owing to fatigue. It places so
much tension on all the muscles of the body, and I do not think it would
do a girl's health any good to cultivate it. Of course if she were
abnormally strong and did not feel the effects of the physical effort,
she would be a tower of strength in the land, and her service would be
an invaluable one.
pair.prefix:
It seems to leave so much open court, of
which your adversary will not be slow to make use.

Use the overhead service for choice, but have an underhand service ready
at your command--it may come in very useful for a change. Remember that
a good-length, well-placed service is better than a very fast one, and
much less tiring in a long match.

source_document.title: Lawn Tennis for Ladies by Mrs. Lambert Chambers
